title: Centre of Our Hopes Thou Art
description: Centre of Our Hopes Thou Art in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 512.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Cen-tre of our hopes thou art, End of our en-larged de-sires; Stamp thine i-mage on our heart, Fill us now with heav-enly fires; Ce-ment-ed by love di-vine, Seal our souls for ev-er thine.

lines: Centre of our hopes thou art,
Stamp thine image on our heart,
Fill us now with heavenly fires;
Seal our souls for ever thine.
All our works in thee be wrought,
Lead us through the paths of peace,
Here prepare to meet our Lord;
Travel hand in hand to heaven!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
